_comment: Two inserts: the face-led hook 0:00-0:04.0 and the 2.15s interrupt at 0:34.4 («And this is where it gets crazy»), which is exactly the two-scene structure the brief asks for and lands inside its 6-7s avatar cap. The avatar does NOT voice the reel — each shot lip-syncs to a whole house clip from public/voiceover/youtube-netflix, so the reel's audio track and durations.ts stay untouched. from/to are seconds inside the mp3 at 1.0x; reelIn/reelOut are where the insert lands in the finished reel at VO_RATE.
_avatar: The podcast-studio look from the «Philipp» avatar group (1b80626e…) — a generated PHOTO avatar, not the Digital Twin. Same character as brands-paying-more and no-it-in-russia. List them: curl -H "X-Api-Key: $HEYGEN_API_KEY" https://api.heygen.com/v2/avatar_group/1b80626e44c945edbad8f5024ce9163b/avatars
_economics: Photo Avatar bills on a different table from a Digital Twin: avatar_iii = $0.0433/s, avatar_iv = $0.05/s. 6.641s on avatar_iv = $0.33, on avatar_iii = $0.29. Both inserts are large in frame (a 600px-wide broadcast plate and a full-bleed push-in) where the mimic carries the shot, so IV — $0.04 more. Quoted from --dry-run and confirmed by the author before generating. User ceiling for this reel: $0.40.
_outputFormat: mp4, not webm. WebM is the only transparency switch, but transparency would throw away the studio — and the studio is what makes the hook read as a broadcast plate rather than a floating head.
_concatAspect: The source photo's native 1920x1080. Cropping to 9:16 happens in Remotion (scenes/HookScene.tsx and scenes/CrazyScene.tsx) so both crops show up on stills and are fixed with one number instead of a paid re-generation.
